title: Filipe Luís faces Luis Enrique at PSG: Ligue 1 debut
seoTitle: Filipe Luis faces Luis Enrique at PSG: Ligue 1 debut
subtitle: Monaco visits Paris Saint‑Germain in a third‑round Ligue 1 match
excerpt: Filipe Luís gets his first European coaching test against Luis Enrique's PSG at Parc des Princes, while Monaco leads the Ligue 1 season.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Filipe Luís arrives at his first major challenge as a coach in Europe, leading Monaco against Luis Enrique's PSG this Friday at 4:05 p.m. (Brasília time). The clash, part of the third round of Ligue 1, pits the Brazilian manager, who guides the league‑leading side, against the current French champions.

Filipe Luís' challenge at Monaco

The Brazilian took charge of Monaco after opening the season with two wins – 1‑0 over Le Havre and 2‑0 against Olympique de Marseille – amassing six points and keeping a clean sheet. In the Conference League qualifiers, the team also recorded four straight victories, boosting confidence ahead of the PSG showdown.

Head‑to‑head history between PSG and Monaco

Filipe Luís already faced PSG as a coach in the 2025 Intercontinental Cup final, when he was in charge of Flamengo. On that occasion, PSG won on penalties after a 1‑1 draw in regular and extra time.

Current state of PSG under Luis Enrique

PSG, led by Luis Enrique, started the season with two 2‑2 draws – against Rennes and Lille – and has yet to record a win in Ligue 1 2026/27. The reinforced squad is missing Nuno Mendes, who is suspended, while U‑S‑M‑Dém‑Bélé is now available again.

Monaco's performance in Ligue 1

Besides topping the table, Monaco has kept a clean sheet in the first two rounds. The side also deals with absences such as Jordan Teze, Matthis Abline, Ansu Fati, Edan Diop, Mohammed Salisu and Takumi Minamino, with Folarin Balogun listed as doubtful for the match.

Expectations for the clash

Filipe Luís pointed out that PSG has had an uneven start, with players returning late from World Cup duties, which could give Monaco a chance to win. Luis Enrique, for his part, praised the Brazilian coach, calling him “brave” and saying he likes trainers who love to play football.

With information from ge, UOL, VEJA.
